applied.title: Subject rescue when only the outcome resolves
applied.change: find_evidence / counter_evidence / statistics returned not_resolvable for 'Semaglutide causes loss of lean muscle mass': the model proposed 'semaglutide treatment' and 'semaglutide therapy' (0 titles each) and the bare drug name was never tried, although MeSH had already placed it. The query builder now audits the bare subject, named entities and MeSH headings, then title-style rephrasings, before giving up. The claim now resolves (54 papers on both sides, 7,386 on the subject).

applied.title: Subset findings are evidence, not 'unrelated'
applied.change: The stance reader labelled 'no reduction in breast cancer risk', 'does not reduce esophageal cancer risk' and 'higher endometrial cancer incidence (HR 1.17)' as unrelated to 'metformin reduces cancer risk', so they never reached counter-evidence. The reading prompt now treats a subset of the claim's outcome or population (one cancer type, one age group, one country) as evidence about the claim: an effect in the claimed direction qualifies, a null or opposite result contradicts.

applied.title: Counter-evidence retrieves dissent on purpose
applied.change: find_counter_evidence re-read the same top-cited documents as find_evidence and filtered them, so on a claim with a strong supporting literature it returned zero dissent. A new fetch_dissent() runs three lanes (typed papers whose own framing is critical / cautionary / problem-identifying, abstracts stating a null / adverse / bias finding, and on health claims PubMed trials and meta-analyses with those findings) and the tool now reads that pool together with the strongest general evidence. Measured on the metformin claim: before, 4 supporting and 0 contradicting; after, 3 verified contradicting meta-analyses (endometrial cancer HR 1.17, 1.09-1.26; esophageal HR 0.88, 0.60-1.28; prostate RR 0.97, 0.80-1.16) beside the supporting JNCI 2024 meta-analysis, and the recommendation changed from 'the documents read support the claim' to 'both supporting and contradictory findings; explain their differences'.

applied.title: Retry for unread documents
applied.change: Under load a whole stance batch can time out, which left 5 of 12 documents in the metformin counter-evidence pool 'unread'. Documents the model returned nothing for are now re-read once in batches of three before being reported as unread.

applied.title: Phrase and term counts no longer overwrite each other
applied.change: The phrase audit returned one dict keyed by name. A topic term derived from a phrase is often the same string, so for 'PM2.5 air pollution increases mortality' the term count for 'all-cause mortality' (0 topic labels) overwrote the phrase count (7,557 titles), the gate dropped the phrase, and the claim was searched with no outcome at all. Term counts now live under their own key.

applied.title: Discovered labels and MeSH must be related to the pole
applied.change: Prism adopts the corpus's own topic labels for a pole by reading the labels on papers whose titles carry the phrase. For a generic outcome those labels describe the co-occurring subject: papers titled '...all-cause mortality' are mostly diet cohorts, so the outcome of 'PM2.5 increases mortality' became 'nutritional studies and diet', 'nutrition and health in aging' and 'health disparities and outcomes'. MeSH resolution had the same failure ('loss of lean muscle mass' -> 'Body Dissatisfaction'). Discovered labels and MeSH headings must now share a content word with the pole's own phrases ('air pollution' -> 'air quality and health impacts' still passes).

applied.title: Unicode hyphens no longer delete a pole
applied.change: The model writes phrases with non-breaking hyphens (U+2011): 'all‑cause mortality', 'post‑acute covid‑19 syndrome'. Those match zero titles, so the audit dropped them and 'PM2.5 increases mortality' was searched with no outcome at all. Every phrase, term, rescue candidate and claim is now normalised to ASCII punctuation before it is audited.

applied.title: Outcome-anchored reading when the title intersection is thin
applied.change: When fewer than the minimum papers carry both poles in their titles, the lane fell back to the subject alone and the reader got the subject's most-cited papers on everything else: 'vitamin D reduces depression' read respiratory-infection, mortality and glycaemic-control meta-analyses and marked all of them unrelated. The reading step now adds an outcome-anchored lane (subject in the title, outcome words or MeSH in the abstract, plus PubMed trials and meta-analyses on a health claim) and ranks on-outcome documents first. Outcome stems come only from the claim's own outcome phrases, not from MeSH qualifiers: 'Depressive Disorder, Treatment-Resistant' produced the stem 'resista', which matched insulin- and antimicrobial-resistance trials. Measured on 'vitamin D supplementation reduces depression symptoms': before, 10 of 10 documents read were unrelated (respiratory infection, mortality, glycaemic control); after, the list is on-topic: two supporting (a 2018 review of vitamin D in major depression, a 2008 RCT in overweight adults) and the null Women's Health Initiative trial as contradicting. On 'PM2.5 air pollution increases mortality' (after the hyphen, phrase/term and label fixes) the reading list now leads with the long-term-exposure mortality cohort in older US adults, premature-mortality projections for India and the cause-specific exposure-response study, and documents that never mention the outcome are no longer read once four on-outcome documents exist.
applied.file: prism/evidence.py (outcome_keywords, fetch_docs outcome_anchor lanes, cache key evidence.profile.v8), read_note on the payload

applied.title: Research geography by author affiliation
applied.change: research.geography ranked research by the PUBLISHING JOURNAL's country, so dengue research looked American, English and Dutch. It now also returns research_authorship: the first author's affiliation country from PubMed, normalised (USA / United States of America / United States, Brasil, PR China, UK...). For dengue that ranks India, the United States, Brazil and Thailand first.

applied.title: Spreadsheet rows must answer the column's question
applied.change: research.table only required that a source name the row, so melanoma's 'response rate' came from a colitis-toxicity meta-analysis and NSCLC's from a proton-pump-inhibitor interaction study. Sources must now also address the column's measure (the question's last distinctive word: response, density, yield), the figure itself must mention it, and a row with no such figure comes back empty with the reason. A row must also contain EVERY distinctive word of its label: with any-word matching, 'lithium iron phosphate' matched every lithium paper and took a unitless 609.4 from a solid-state catholyte study.

applied.title: Showcase harness: the models saw truncated news panels
applied.change: Not a server bug, a test bug: the digest that hands Prism results to Claude and ChatGPT cut news.overview at a character budget, which removed geography, publishers and headlines. The digest now keeps every panel and drops only repeated fields (7.5k characters instead of a truncated 16k), and every pulse comparison was re-run.

applied.title: Radar 'new work' is the work the field is reading
applied.change: research.radar listed whatever the evidence fetcher's recency lanes returned. On 'mrna vaccine' that was HPV, RSV-protein and adenoviral vaccine papers, because PubMed matched the broad MeSH heading 'Vaccines'. On quantum computing it was a handful of minor 2025 papers, with the error-correction milestones absent. New work is now the most-cited typed papers since the start year whose title carries one of the subject's own phrases, with each paper's orientation. After: the 2023+ list for 'mrna vaccine' is ten mRNA papers led by 'A Comprehensive Review of mRNA Vaccines' (379 citations), lipid-nanoparticle immunogenicity (331), spike protein in post-vaccine myocarditis (222) and mRNA vaccines in cancer therapy, each with its orientation.

applied.title: A geography scope is applied, not just stored
applied.change: research.brief(topic, geo='india') stored the place on the query object and never applied it, so 'childhood obesity in India' reported the world's obesity literature (168,958 research papers, 267,064 PubMed records) with India's share at zero. The predicate now scopes every corpus. A paper counts when its title names the place (word prefix, so 'Indian' counts) or its authors' institutions are there, and a news article when it is about the place. PubMed childhood-obesity papers scoped to India: 122. research.geography still ranks countries over the unscoped claim.

applied.title: Tool routing: fact-checks go to research_audit, not drive
applied.change: In the live audit session ChatGPT chose drive ('audit this draft' was one of its advertised briefs). drive runs in the background and returns a job_id; the client never polled it and told the user Prism had found no sources, while Claude called research_audit and corrected the draft from the 2017 BMJ umbrella review (cardiovascular RR 0.85, not a 50% reduction). drive's description now sends plain fact-checks to research_audit or find_evidence, and research_audit's first line says it is the tool for 'check this article'.
applied.file: prism_mcp.py (drive, research_audit docstrings = MCP tool descriptions)

applied.title: Evidence card never shows an unrelated document as the strongest evidence
applied.change: When every document read was labelled unrelated, evidence_card fell back to the highest-tier document anyway. 'Microplastics cause cancer' got a card for a meta-analysis of microbial biofilms on microplastics (rated very_high), and 'screen time causes ADHD' got an autism meta-analysis. The card now uses only grounded documents that support, contradict or qualify the claim, and otherwise says how many were read and that none speaks to it.

applied.title: Draft audit: no sentence padding in search phrases, and a deeper default in the showcase
applied.change: The audit requires multi-word phrases so a bare noun cannot match a whole field, and the model met the rule by padding: 'coffee is', 'coffee also', 'caffeine raises', 'drinking three cups a day'. Those match almost no titles, and the audit reported no_literature on heart disease and blood pressure, two of the largest literatures in the corpus. Padding verbs, quantities and filler are now stripped, the prompt asks for title-style phrasing ('coffee consumption'), and a single concept is kept when the claim also has an outcome to pair it with. The showcase now runs the audit with deep=3 (a full evidence read on the three weakest claims), which adds direction and effect sizes.
applied.file: prism/article.py (_PAD, _clean_phrases, extraction prompt, cache key audit.extraction.v2), showcase/capture.py

applied.title: A failed naming call no longer degrades the whole query
applied.change: When the model call that names a claim's two poles failed under load, query.build fell back to the sentence's own bigrams ('metformin reduces', 'reduces cancer') with no outcome pole, and cached that degraded object for 12 hours. Re-captured during a busy hour, the metformin page read kidney-disease and pregnancy papers and dropped from a Prism win to a loss. The naming call is now retried twice with backoff, and a fallback build is never cached.

open.title: Slow tools outlast the Codex/ChatGPT client's wait
open.note: In live sessions ChatGPT (Codex CLI) called search_research / compare_claims / research_table, then ended its turn before the call returned ('Prism's research search has not returned yet'), even with tool_timeout_sec=900, while the cluster was under heavy load. Cold evidence and table calls take 1-7 minutes there. Two mitigations exist today: the 12-hour cache (warm calls return in under a second) and system.request + system.request_status (submit, then poll). The next step is to have the long tools return a request_id automatically past ~60 s so every client gets the polling path.

open.title: historical_analysis has a 20-second default budget
open.note: Under a loaded cluster the yearly title-count scan over 401M works exceeds the 20 s default and returns TimeoutError, and the parameter is capped at 30 s. The showcase uses the 30 s maximum; the default should adapt to cluster load or fall back to the 105M-row typed table.

open.title: Attention gap drifts to neighbouring materials topics
open.note: research.radar's under_covered list for green hydrogen includes 'Magnesium Alloys', 'Aluminum Alloys Composites' and 'Rare-earth and actinide compounds' next to the relevant 'Hydrogen Storage and Materials'. The topic labels are taken from the subject's paper set without a relevance check; the same lexical/co-occurrence gate used for discovered labels should apply.

open.title: Library gaps suggest off-field classics
open.note: For an AI-ethics reading list, highly_cited_missing includes 'Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision'. The candidate pool is the list's citation neighbourhood, which for ML-adjacent ethics papers pulls in core ML architecture papers; candidates should be filtered to the list's own themes.
